events.title: Tilly's Imperial-Spanish army captures Mannheim
events.description: In the Thirty Years' War, the Imperial-Spanish army of Johann Tserclaes, Count of Tilly, took Mannheim from Protestant troops under the Englishman Sir Horace Vere. Tilly, a Walloon general, commanded the army of the Catholic League.
events.html: In the Thirty Years' War, the Imperial-Spanish army of Johann Tserclaes, Count of Tilly, took Mannheim from Protestant troops under the Englishman Sir Horace Vere. Tilly, a Walloon general, commanded the army of the Catholic League.

events.title: Washington issues his farewell orders to the Continental Army
events.description: From Rocky Hill, New Jersey, George Washington issued his Farewell Orders to the Armies of the United States. Weeks later he resigned his commission, setting a precedent of civilian control.
events.html: From Rocky Hill, New Jersey, George Washington issued his Farewell Orders to the Armies of the United States. Weeks later he resigned his commission, setting a precedent of civilian control.

events.title: North and South Dakota become US states
events.description: President Benjamin Harrison signed proclamations admitting North and South Dakota on the same day. He shuffled the papers so no one would know which was signed first.
events.html: President Benjamin Harrison signed proclamations admitting North and South Dakota on the same day. He shuffled the papers so no one would know which was signed first.

events.title: The Boers begin the siege of Ladysmith
events.description: In the Second Boer War, Boer forces besieged the British garrison at Ladysmith in Natal. The siege lasted 118 days, until Sir Redvers Buller's army relieved the garrison on 28 February 1900 after costly battles at Colenso and Spion Kop.
events.html: In the Second Boer War, Boer forces besieged the British garrison at Ladysmith in Natal. The siege lasted 118 days, until Sir Redvers Buller's army relieved the garrison on 28 February 1900 after costly battles at Colenso and Spion Kop.

events.title: The Balfour Declaration backs a Jewish home in Palestine
events.description: Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour wrote to Lord Rothschild that Britain favoured 'a national home for the Jewish people' in Palestine, without prejudice to existing non-Jewish communities. Its consequences still shape the region.
events.html: Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour wrote to Lord Rothschild that Britain favoured 'a national home for the Jewish people' in Palestine, without prejudice to existing non-Jewish communities. Its consequences still shape the region.

events.title: Haile Selassie is crowned Emperor of Ethiopia
events.description: Ras Tafari Makonnen was crowned Emperor Haile Selassie I in Addis Ababa before foreign dignitaries. He ruled Ethiopia, with an interruption during Italian occupation, until his overthrow in 1974.
events.html: Ras Tafari Makonnen was crowned Emperor Haile Selassie I in Addis Ababa before foreign dignitaries. He ruled Ethiopia, with an interruption during Italian occupation, until his overthrow in 1974.

events.title: The BBC launches the world's first regular high-definition TV service
events.description: From Alexandra Palace in north London, the BBC began a regular public television service in what was then called high definition. It was suspended during the Second World War and resumed in 1946.
events.html: From Alexandra Palace in north London, the BBC began a regular public television service in what was then called high definition. It was suspended during the Second World War and resumed in 1946.

events.title: The first crew moves into the International Space Station
events.description: Expedition 1, an American astronaut and two Russian cosmonauts, docked at the International Space Station. Since then the station has been continuously occupied by humans.
events.html: Expedition 1, an American astronaut and two Russian cosmonauts, docked at the International Space Station. Since then the station has been continuously occupied by humans.
